name: US
title: US Political Compass Test 2026 | CoreOpinion
desc: Where do you stand in American politics? 70 statements to see your alignment with Democrats, Republicans, Libertarians and the Greens, plus your framing bias.
keywords: US political quiz, American political compass test, Democrat Republican quiz, where do I stand in American politics, political alignment test USA, libertarian quiz, US party quiz 2026, am I a Democrat or Republican, political ideology test America

dem.name: Democrat
dem.desc: Your answers most closely match the Democratic Party platform. You tend to favour government intervention to reduce inequality, protect civil rights, and address climate change.

rep.name: Republican
rep.desc: Your answers most closely match the Republican Party platform. You tend to favour lower taxes, strong borders, traditional values, and a powerful national defence.

lib.name: Libertarian
lib.desc: Your answers most closely match the Libertarian Party platform. You want maximum freedom in both economic and personal life, with minimal government intervention in either.

grn.name: Green
grn.desc: Your answers most closely match the Green Party platform. You prioritise environmental justice, corporate accountability, and a fundamental restructuring of the economy.

ind.name: Independent
ind.desc: Your answers do not strongly align with any single party. You hold mixed views that draw from multiple traditions, typical of the roughly 40% of Americans who identify as independents.

bank.q: The US should have government-guaranteed healthcare for all, even if it means higher taxes.
bank.ctx: This supports a government-guaranteed healthcare system (like 'Medicare for All') funded by taxes, so everyone is covered regardless of income.

bank.q: Government-run healthcare means rationing and lost freedom; the private system should stay.
bank.ctx: This defends America's mainly private, insurance-based healthcare, warning that a government system would ration care and reduce choice.

bank.q: Illegal immigration is an invasion that must be stopped with mass deportations and a border wall.
bank.ctx: This is a hardline border position: treating illegal immigration as an invasion to be stopped with mass deportations and a border wall.

bank.q: Immigrants, documented or not, are part of America, and mass deportation is cruel and un-American.
bank.ctx: This is the pro-immigrant view: that immigrants, legal or not, are part of American society and mass deportation is cruel and against American ideals.

bank.q: Undocumented immigrants who have lived here for years should get a path to citizenship.
bank.ctx: This supports giving undocumented immigrants who have lived in the US for years a legal route to eventually become citizens.

bank.q: Rewarding people who broke the law with citizenship just encourages more illegal immigration.
bank.ctx: This opposes such an amnesty, arguing it rewards breaking the law and encourages more illegal immigration.

bank.q: Abortion is a fundamental right, and overturning Roe v. Wade was a grave injustice.
bank.ctx: This is the pro-choice position. Roe v. Wade was the 1973 Supreme Court ruling that protected abortion nationwide until it was overturned in 2022, returning the decision to each state.

bank.q: Abortion is the taking of an innocent life, and states are right to restrict or ban it.
bank.ctx: This is the pro-life position: that abortion takes an innocent life, so states are right to restrict or ban it now that Roe v. Wade is gone.

bank.q: The Second Amendment is nearly absolute; gun ownership should not be restricted.
bank.ctx: The Second Amendment is the part of the US Constitution protecting the right to bear arms. This treats that right as almost absolute, opposing gun restrictions.

bank.q: America’s gun bloodshed demands real restrictions, including bans on assault-style weapons.
bank.ctx: This is the gun-control view: that America's high rate of gun deaths justifies real limits, such as banning assault-style weapons.

bank.q: Donald Trump is a threat to American democracy.
bank.ctx: This states that Donald Trump, the Republican president, endangers American democracy — a common view among his critics, especially after the January 6th Capitol riot.

bank.q: The real threat to democracy is a establishment that weaponizes the courts against Trump and his voters.
bank.ctx: This is the pro-Trump counter-view: that the real danger is a political and legal 'establishment' using the courts to go after Trump and his supporters.

bank.q: The ultra-wealthy and big corporations should pay far more in taxes.
bank.ctx: This supports raising taxes substantially on the richest Americans and large corporations to fund public spending and reduce inequality.

bank.q: Raising taxes on job creators and businesses just kills investment and growth.
bank.ctx: This opposes higher taxes on the wealthy and business, arguing they discourage the investment and hiring that drive economic growth.

bank.q: Climate change is a crisis, and the US must transform its economy to fight it.
bank.ctx: This treats climate change as an urgent crisis requiring major, even costly, changes to the US economy and energy system.

bank.q: Climate alarmism is being used to justify a costly government takeover of the economy.
bank.ctx: This is climate-policy scepticism: the argument that climate fears are exaggerated to justify expensive government control over the economy.

bank.q: Systemic racism is real and America must take active steps to address it.
bank.ctx: 'Systemic racism' means discrimination built into laws and institutions, not just individual prejudice. This holds it is real and must be actively tackled.

bank.q: The obsession with systemic racism is itself divisive and teaches Americans to see race everywhere.
bank.ctx: This pushes back on the systemic-racism idea, arguing the focus on it is itself divisive and makes people see everything through the lens of race.

bank.q: Some races are simply more intelligent or capable than others.
bank.ctx: This is a statement of racial supremacism — the belief that some races are inherently more intelligent or capable than others. Mainstream science rejects it, and it is historically tied to ideologies like Nazism and systems like apartheid.

bank.q: There is no hierarchy of races; the idea is pseudo-science with a shameful history.
bank.ctx: This is the principle of human equality: that no race is inherently smarter or more capable, and that the idea of a racial hierarchy is discredited pseudo-science with a shameful history.

bank.q: The answer to crime is more police and tougher sentences, not less.
bank.ctx: This favours a tough-on-crime approach: more police and longer prison sentences rather than a softer response.

bank.q: Mass incarceration and aggressive policing have failed; the money should go to prevention.
bank.ctx: This argues the tough approach has failed — America jails more people than any country — and money should go to preventing crime instead.

bank.q: Trans Americans should be able to change their legal gender and access gender-affirming care.
bank.ctx: This supports transgender rights: letting trans Americans change their legal gender and get 'gender-affirming' medical care.

bank.q: Biological sex is real, and children especially should not be pushed toward gender transition.
bank.ctx: This is the gender-critical view: that biological sex is real and that children in particular should not be steered toward gender transition.

bank.q: The federal minimum wage should be raised to at least 15 dollars an hour.
bank.ctx: The federal minimum wage is the legal lowest hourly pay, stuck at $7.25 since 2009. This supports raising it to at least $15.

bank.q: Forcing wages up by law just closes small businesses and destroys entry-level jobs.
bank.ctx: This opposes a big minimum-wage rise, arguing it would force small businesses to close and cut entry-level jobs.

bank.q: Student debt is crushing a generation and much of it should be cancelled.
bank.ctx: This supports cancelling much of Americans' student loan debt, which totals over a trillion dollars and burdens many graduates.

bank.q: Cancelling student debt forces people who never went to college to pay for those who did.
bank.ctx: This opposes student-debt cancellation, arguing it is unfair to make people who never went to college pay for those who did.

bank.q: Programs like Social Security and Medicare should be expanded, not cut.
bank.ctx: Social Security (pensions) and Medicare (healthcare for the elderly) are big federal programs. This supports expanding rather than cutting them.

bank.q: Entitlement spending is bankrupting the country and must be reined in.
bank.ctx: This warns that spending on these 'entitlement' programs is unaffordable and must be reined in to control the national debt.

bank.q: The US should keep arming Ukraine against Russia for as long as it takes.
bank.ctx: This supports continuing US military aid to Ukraine in its war against Russia's invasion, for as long as needed.

bank.q: Endless funding for foreign wars is money that should be spent on Americans at home.
bank.ctx: This opposes open-ended funding for the war, arguing the money should be spent on Americans at home instead.

bank.q: The US should continue its strong military and financial support for Israel.
bank.ctx: This supports continued strong US military and financial backing for Israel, a long-standing American ally.

bank.q: The US should stop bankrolling Israel and condition or end its military aid.
bank.ctx: This wants the US to reduce, condition, or end its military aid to Israel, often over its conduct toward Palestinians.

bank.q: Tariffs to protect American industry and jobs are worth the higher prices.
bank.ctx: Tariffs are taxes on imported goods. This supports using them to protect American factories and jobs, even if it raises prices for shoppers.

bank.q: Tariffs are a tax on American families and start trade wars that hurt everyone.
bank.ctx: This opposes tariffs, arguing they raise prices for American families and trigger damaging trade wars.

bank.q: America is a Christian nation and its laws should reflect Christian values.
bank.ctx: This is Christian nationalism: the view that America is fundamentally a Christian country whose laws should reflect Christian values.

bank.q: The separation of church and state is fundamental; religion has no place in law.
bank.ctx: This defends the separation of church and state — a founding US principle — keeping religion out of law and government.

bank.q: Islam is not compatible with American values.
bank.ctx: This argues that Islam clashes with American values. Supporters cite security and social concerns; critics call it religious prejudice.

bank.q: Muslim Americans are full citizens, and their faith deserves the same respect as any other.
bank.ctx: This holds that Muslim Americans are full and equal citizens whose religion deserves the same respect as any other.

bank.q: Free speech is under threat from cancel culture and campus censorship.
bank.ctx: 'Cancel culture' refers to people losing jobs or being shamed for their opinions. This argues free speech is being suppressed, especially on campuses.

bank.q: The free-speech panic is overblown cover for people who just want to say bigoted things without consequences.
bank.ctx: This argues the free-speech alarm is overblown, and is really cover for people who want to say bigoted things without facing criticism.

bank.q: Diversity, equity, and inclusion programs have gone too far and should be scrapped.
bank.ctx: DEI stands for Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion — workplace programs to promote underrepresented groups. This argues they have gone too far and should be scrapped.

bank.q: DEI programs exist because discrimination is real, and scrapping them just protects the powerful.
bank.ctx: This defends DEI programs, arguing they exist because discrimination is real and that ending them mainly protects those already in power.

bank.q: Marijuana should be legal nationwide and drug use treated as a health issue.
bank.ctx: This supports legalising marijuana across the country and treating drug use as a health matter rather than a crime.

bank.q: Loosening drug laws has fueled addiction and disorder, and it should be reversed.
bank.ctx: This opposes loosening drug laws, arguing it has fuelled addiction and public disorder and should be reversed.

bank.q: Terminally ill adults should have the legal right to medically assisted death.
bank.ctx: 'Medically assisted death' lets terminally ill adults choose to end their lives with medical help. This supports making it a legal right.

bank.q: Assisted dying puts pressure on the vulnerable and crosses a line society should not cross.
bank.ctx: This opposes assisted dying, warning it could pressure vulnerable or disabled people and crosses a moral line.

bank.q: Protecting the environment should take priority over expanding oil, gas, and coal.
bank.ctx: This puts protecting the environment ahead of expanding fossil fuels like oil, gas, and coal.

bank.q: Energy independence and cheap power matter more than blocking drilling and pipelines.
bank.ctx: This prioritises cheap, home-produced energy and energy independence over restrictions on drilling and pipelines.

bank.q: Government should intervene heavily to make housing affordable, including rent control.
bank.ctx: This supports strong government action on housing costs, including rent control (legal caps on how much rents can rise).

bank.q: Rent control and mandates make the housing shortage worse; deregulation lets the market build.
bank.ctx: This argues rent control and mandates make housing shortages worse, and that cutting regulations to let builders build is the fix.

bank.q: The Electoral College should be abolished in favor of the national popular vote.
bank.ctx: The Electoral College is the system that can let a candidate win the presidency without winning the most votes nationally. This wants it abolished for a national popular vote.

bank.q: The Electoral College protects smaller states and should be kept.
bank.ctx: This defends the Electoral College, arguing it protects the influence of smaller states in presidential elections.

bank.q: Universal background checks and red-flag laws are common-sense and should be federal law.
bank.ctx: This supports federal gun-safety rules: background checks for all buyers and 'red-flag' laws that let courts remove guns from dangerous people.

bank.q: Background-check and red-flag schemes are a slippery slope to confiscation and should be resisted.
bank.ctx: This opposes those measures, seeing them as a step toward eventually confiscating law-abiding people's guns.

bank.q: Big Tech and monopolies should be broken up and tightly regulated.
bank.ctx: This supports breaking up and tightly regulating giant technology companies and other monopolies to curb their power.

bank.q: Heavy-handed regulation of successful companies just kills the innovation that made America rich.
bank.ctx: This argues heavy regulation of successful companies stifles the innovation that made the US economy strong.

bank.q: The US spends too much on its military and should cut the defense budget.
bank.ctx: The US has by far the world's largest military budget. This argues it spends too much and should cut defense spending.

bank.q: A strong, well-funded military is what keeps America and its allies safe.
bank.ctx: This defends high military spending as what keeps America and its allies safe.

bank.q: Children should be taught pride in America’s history, not mainly its sins.
bank.ctx: This favours patriotic education: teaching children pride in America's history rather than focusing on its wrongs.

bank.q: A country that hides slavery and its other crimes from students is lying to them.
bank.ctx: This supports teaching the darker parts of US history, like slavery, arguing that hiding them misleads students.

bank.q: Birthright citizenship for children born on US soil should be ended.
bank.ctx: Birthright citizenship means anyone born on US soil is automatically a citizen. This wants that ended.

bank.q: Birthright citizenship is in the Constitution and a core American principle that must be protected.
bank.ctx: This defends birthright citizenship as a constitutional guarantee (the 14th Amendment) and a core American principle.

bank.q: The poor and unemployed face too many hurdles; the safety net should be stronger and easier to access.
bank.ctx: This argues the poor and unemployed face too many hurdles, and that welfare and support should be stronger and easier to get.

bank.q: Welfare too easily becomes a trap, and work requirements protect taxpayers who fund it.
bank.ctx: This argues welfare can trap people in dependency, and that work requirements protect the taxpayers who fund it.

bank.q: Long-standing traditions carry the wisdom of generations and should not be discarded lightly.
bank.ctx: This is the conservative view of tradition: that long-standing customs and institutions hold accumulated wisdom, so we should be cautious about sweeping them away for something new.

bank.q: Worshipping tradition just lets the dead govern the living and blocks necessary change.
bank.ctx: This is the progressive reply: that clinging to tradition for its own sake lets the past dictate to the present and blocks change that is needed.

bank.q: A good society depends more on personal responsibility than on government help.
bank.ctx: This reflects a right-leaning value: that a good society rests mainly on individuals taking responsibility for their own lives, rather than leaning on government.

bank.q: Blaming individuals for problems the system creates is how the comfortable excuse others’ suffering.
bank.ctx: This reflects a left-leaning value: that many problems are caused by unfair systems, so blaming individuals lets the comfortable look past suffering they may benefit from.

heroSub: 70 statements on the issues defining America right now: healthcare, immigration, abortion, guns, and the economy. Every position is asked twice with opposite framing, revealing both your party alignment and your framing bias.
partyStripHtml:
Democrat
Your answers most closely match the Democratic Party platform. You tend to favour government intervention to reduce inequality, protect civil rights, and address climate change.
Republican
Your answers most closely match the Republican Party platform. You tend to favour lower taxes, strong borders, traditional values, and a powerful national defence.
Libertarian
Your answers most closely match the Libertarian Party platform. You want maximum freedom in both economic and personal life, with minimal government intervention in either.
Green
Your answers most closely match the Green Party platform. You prioritise environmental justice, corporate accountability, and a fundamental restructuring of the economy.
